feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Drones buzz overhead, troops hunker underground in Ukraine's hellish kill zone
entry.summary: The front line in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the kill zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.

entry.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
entry.summary: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.

entry.title: Imran Khan supporters march in Pakistan to demand his release after talks failed
entry.summary: Talks between Khan's party and the government failed two days ago. Besides Khan's release, protesters demand his transfer to a hospital and family visits.

entry.title: SCOTUS hears major climate change case. And, Brazil's presidential race goes to runoff
entry.summary: The Supreme Court is set to hear a blockbuster climate change case that could affect more than just climate issues. And, Brazil's presidential race is too close to call.

entry.title: FlyDubai attacker intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, investigation finds
entry.summary: The ongoing investigation has found the attacker intended to crash the plane into Israel's Ben Gurion International Airport, a person familiar with the matter but not authorized to speak publicly told NPR.

entry.title: U.S. Marine suspected in woman's death arrested in Japan
entry.summary: A U.S. Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa, prompting renewed Japanese criticism of the conduct of American military personnel.

entry.title: Nobel medicine prize goes to 3 scientists for research into brain activity
entry.summary: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.

entry.title: Former Prince Andrew files legal action to quash warrants that led to residence searches
entry.summary: A judicial spokesperson confirmed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had filed a claim with the High Court in London and a hearing would take place Thursday.

entry.title: Spain's prime minister calls early elections as pressure mounts over housing crisis
entry.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced early elections Monday after his government suffered a bruising legislative defeat last week on emergency measures related to the country's housing crisis.

entry.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine escalate as its drones target bridges in Kyiv
entry.summary: Russia's jet-powered drones are targeting bridges in the Ukrainian capital, an escalation after more than a month of day-and-night strikes that have left Kyiv feeling almost like a frontline city.
